items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: he -- he had a pianist who traveled with him, Putney Dandridge

ctx.x: they were great singers, but they were competent, and they looked good; they were young, and they were nice looking girls, and they dressed well, and they looked nice. And they made quite a few tours with us, theater tours they did mostly, and we backed several big stars when I was with that band.

One of the stars we backed was Bill Robinson, Bojangles. We did about 20 -- about 22 weeks of theaters with Bill Robinson, and our main thing was to back him, and he -- he had a pianist who traveled with him, Putney Dandridge and, of course, we -- there were certain recordings that we did that he liked, and he liked to tap dance to these things. One of them was Ain't She Sweet. And we used to sing that and play it softly, very softly, and he would come out and tap dance to it, and he liked -- For Pancers Only. We…

But we played it very soft, because he was a great artist, I thought, you know. I always used to watch this man perform, and he really had something going there. He could really reach the people. We played lots of theaters with him all through the Middle West, through Texas. There was a chain of theaters through Texas -- I think Majestic Theaters, I think, was the name; I'm not sure of that chain -- and we played quite a few theaters throughout the country. We did 22 straight weeks of theaters with him,…
